title: check format verifies one of the languages fmt formats, while claiming the project
body:
# 0003: check format verifies one of the languages fmt formats, while claiming the project

## Tags

check, fmt, gates, false-green, D21, WP-10

## Summary

`fmt` has four language arms -- `elixir`, `rust`, `swift`, `md`. `check format` has one, `mix format --check-formatted`. So in a project declaring more than one formattable language, `check all` reports "all check options passed" having never looked at the formatting of any language but Elixir, while `fmt all` would reformat all of them.

The option is named `format` and its catalogue summary is "Formatting is up to date". That is a claim about the project, not about its Elixir. Found during WP-10 preparation, by asking a mixed-language fixture what it was actually offered.

Not raised against a project's config -- a project can override the command line. Raised against devbin, because the DEFAULT gate asserts more than it verified, and because Conflab's existing launcher checks all three.

## Reproduction

A scratch install declaring `elixir`, `rust` and `swift`, and nothing else:

```
$ bin/devbin help fmt
Options:
  elixir                Format Elixir sources
  rust                  Format Rust sources
  swift                 Format Swift sources in place
  md                    Format Markdown -- root only unless given paths
  all                   every option above, one pass

$ bin/devbin help check
Options:
  compile               Compile with warnings as errors
  format                Formatting is up to date        <-- one arm, elixir only
  deps                  No unused dependencies
  clippy                Clippy lints as errors
  toolchain             The .tool-versions pin matches what is running
  critic                Rules of the road, per declared language
  all                   every option above, one pass
```

The catalogue rows, which is where the asymmetry lives:

```
check.format     elixir  generic  FORMAT    -  mix format --check-formatted | Formatting is up to date
fmt.elixir       elixir  generic  FMTEX     -  mix format   | Format Elixir sources
fmt.rust         rust    generic  FMTRS     -  cargo fmt    | Format Rust sources
fmt.swift        swift   generic  FMTSWIFT  -  @builtin     | Format Swift sources in place
fmt.md           any     generic  FMTMD     -  @builtin     | Format Markdown -- root only unless given paths
```

## Root Cause

Not an oversight in the table -- there is a test holding the two together, and it encodes the gap rather than catching it. `tests/unit/buildfmt.bats:216`:

```bash
@test "the formatting gate and the formatter agree by construction" {
  applied="$(builtin_option_run fmt elixir)"
  verified="$(builtin_option_run check format)"
  [ "$verified" = "$applied --check-formatted" ] || fail ...
}
```

The test is green and it is correct about what it checks: the Elixir arms agree. Its NAME claims more -- "the formatting gate and the formatter agree by construction" -- and reading it is what makes the gap invisible, because it looks like the relationship is already policed. Its own comment names the risk exactly one level too shallow: "two command lines that are supposed to be the same thing plus a flag will drift the moment one is edited alone". The drift that already exists is that there are FOUR command lines on one side and one on the other.

This is D21 half-implemented. D21 rules that `fmt --check` is `check format` and only one of them ships; the non-mutating half shipped for one language.

## Impact

A green `check all` that has not checked what its own option name says it checked. `check.format` is `elixir`-scoped, so the gate is inactive in a rust-only or swift-only project -- which is honest, since it claims nothing. The damage is in MIXED projects, where declaring Elixir activates the gate and the gate then silently covers only Elixir.

Conflab is exactly that shape. Its current `check_format` runs `mix format --check-formatted` AND `cargo fmt --check` over both crates, so migrating onto the devbin default is a coverage regression on a live project: same exit code, same empty seal, two languages no longer examined. This is the instance AC-10.9 was written for, and it is why that AC asks the equivalence evidence to compare what each gate EXAMINED rather than what it returned.

Devbin's own build is unaffected -- it declares `shell` only, so `check.format` is not active here and `check all` does not offer it.

## Proposed Fix

Follow the precedent already in the same table. `check.critic` is `any` + `@builtin` and loops over the declared languages ("Rules of the road, per declared language"); `check.format` should be the same shape, backed by a `builtin_check_format` beside `builtin_check_critic` and `builtin_check_toolchain` in `lib/cmd/check`. The command surface does not change -- `check format` stays one option -- and each arm derives from the matching `fmt` row so the two cannot drift.

The existing test then generalises: assert the relationship for EVERY `fmt` arm the project declares, not just `fmt elixir`.

**One decision this needs from the owner, because it has blast radius.** Making the row `any` activates the gate everywhere, including projects with no formattable language. The project's own doctrine says a gate that examines nothing must FAIL, but that would light up in any shell-only project -- devbin included -- which does not have a formatter to point at. The choices are to scope the row to the languages that have a formatter arm, or to keep it `any` and have it fail loudly where nothing is formattable. That is a ruling, not an implementation detail, which is why this is raised rather than fixed.

## Related

- ST0001 WP-10 -- AC-10.9, written for this instance before it was confirmed
- ST0001 `design.md` D21 -- `fmt --check` is `check format`, and only one of them ships
- 0002 -- the other WP-10-preparation finding, same class: a success path asserting more than it verified

## Resolutions

Fixed 2026-08-08 on hv's ruling. The open question in the proposal was whether an `any`-scoped gate should fail where nothing is formattable; hv's answer was that "there is nothing to format" is a legitimate outcome, and it is -- the doctrine's target is a gate that SILENTLY examines nothing it was asked to, not one reporting a determinate fact about the project's declared languages.

**The gate.** `check.format` is `any` + `@builtin`, backed by `builtin_check_format` -- shaped after `builtin_check_critic`, which had already answered the same question for rule-checking: one pass per declared language, nothing offered the project did not ask for. A project with no formattable language says so and passes.

**The missing-tool rule stays inverted from `fmt`**, and this is now the one place that asymmetry is implemented rather than described: `fmt` skips a missing formatter loudly and exits 0 because it asserts no verdict; the gate dies, because exiting 0 having examined nothing is the false green. That is not in tension with "nothing to check" passing -- there the gate could not check something it WAS asked to; here it was asked to check nothing.

**The relationship lives in one place.** `builtin_fmt_check_run` (`lib/builtins`) derives each check arm from the `fmt` row it verifies, so editing `fmt rust` cannot leave the gate on a stale command line. The check verbs are not a uniform suffix -- `--check-formatted`, `--check`, `--lint` -- so it is a case, not concatenation. `swift` returns `@builtin` because `fmt.swift` is itself a find feeding xargs with no command line to derive from.

**Markdown is deliberately excluded, verified rather than assumed.** `prettier --check` fails on this repository's own `README.md` and `usage-rules.md`; the diff shows prettier re-padding table columns, and this project hand-aligns them. A gate that goes red on files kept that way on purpose is wrong by construction. The exclusion is asserted by a test, and that test was proven to discriminate by temporarily giving `md` a check form and watching it fail -- it had been passing only because the function did not exist yet.

**The old test was half the defect.** `buildfmt.bats`'s "the formatting gate and the formatter agree by construction" bound `check format` to `fmt elixir`: green, true of the arm it checked, silent about the other three, and reassuring enough to read that nobody looked further. It now asserts COVERAGE -- every `fmt` arm with a language must have a check arm -- so the same gap cannot reopen.

AC-15.6 was broadened to match, and the change recorded on the AC line itself; its original wording named `fmt elixir` alone, which was the gap in contract form.

Nine tests. Five verified RED against the pre-fix code. Two are guards that were already green and are labelled as such in the coverage note rather than counted as proof.

Devbin's own build is unaffected, for a correct reason rather than luck: it declares its `check` options explicitly in config, which displaces the catalogue's option set. Gates green -- `check all` clean, `test all` 474 with an empty seal.
